claims.claim: Nebius sits between hyperscaler AI demand and physical GPU/datacenter capacity; the disclosed five-year Meta commitment provides an offtake signal that can support financing and capacity deployment.
The successor bottleneck is execution: power, sites, GPUs, networking and timely commissioning must convert contracted demand into usable compute before financing obligations overwhelm economics.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Nebius can aggregate scarce AI infrastructure, but depends on upstream GPUs, power and datacenter delivery.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Long-duration demand supports downside resilience while concentrated buildout creates schedule and utilization sensitivity.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Customers can shift among hyperscalers, specialist GPU clouds or owned infrastructure if relative economics change.

risks.risk: Power, GPU supply, construction and commissioning become successor bottlenecks after demand is contracted.

causalEdges.mechanism: long-duration offtake supports buildout and financing
causalEdges.falsifier: customers reduce commitments or capacity delivery slips materially

causalEdges.mechanism: secured debt funds assets against expected contracted cash flows
causalEdges.falsifier: deployment economics fail to cover debt and operating obligations

unknowns.unknown: Contract margins, customer concentration economics and long-run utilization are not established by current evidence.

claims.claim: Large contracted demand reduces pure demand uncertainty but increases concentration and delivery risk because substantial capacity must be built on schedule for a small number of very large customers.

Secured asset-backed debt lowers equity-only funding dependence but adds fixed obligations; the company claim that facility plus customer cash flows covers more than 100% of underlying deployment capex does not establish attractive project returns.

factors.name: financingRisk
factors.basis: Contract-backed secured debt funds growth while increasing fixed claims on project cash flows.

factors.name: concentrationRisk
factors.basis: Very large hyperscaler commitments can make customer-specific delivery and renewal outcomes material.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Contract value should not be treated as equivalent to revenue, margin or free cash flow.

risks.risk: Customer concentration and buildout timing can turn contracted backlog into financing stress if delivery slips.
GPU-cloud competition and hyperscaler self-build can pressure renewal economics and pricing.

causalEdges.mechanism: delayed capacity postpones contracted cash flow while debt and build costs persist
causalEdges.falsifier: timely commissioning and contracted cash generation consistently cover obligations

contradictions.claim: High demand visibility versus uncertain project returns
contradictions.resolution: The contracts support demand visibility but disclosed evidence does not establish margin, return on capital or renewal economics.

unknowns.unknown: Exact contract termination rights, margin profile and customer-level concentration are not established here.
